correctness.rationale: For every binary host with r ones and Z=k-2+q zeros, each chosen pair of ones covers at most binom(q+2,2) two-marker targets; union over binom(r,2) pairs gives the triangular lower bound. The spaced-marker host W=(0^h1)^{ceil((k-2)/h)+1}0^e, e=k-2-(ceil((k-2)/h)-1)h, covers all targets by choosing marker indices to cover prefix/middle and leaving >=c zeros after; count its length. Direct independent subsequence checks for all k=3..19 and h=1..5 and exact comparison of old/new lower bounds confirm finite instances. This proves only Θ(sqrt k) with lower constant 2*2^{1/4}, upper 2sqrt2, not a sharp limit.
